A horizontal scale of the IUCN Red List categories as a row of coloured boxes from left to right, getting darker towards extinction: Least Concern (green), Near Threatened (light green), Vulnerable (yellow), Endangered (orange), Critically Endangered (red), Extinct in the Wild (dark purple), Extinct (black). A bracket over Vulnerable, Endangered and Critically Endangered. Small simple animal icons under some boxes: a Cross River gorilla under Critically Endangered and a drill under Endangered. Separate grey boxes at the side for Data Deficient and Not Evaluated.

An outline map of Nigeria with state boundaries shown faintly. Green shaded areas or markers show the locations of the national parks: Kainji Lake (west, on the River Niger in Niger and Kwara States, with the lake drawn in blue), Old Oyo (south-west, in Oyo State), Okomu (south, in Edo State), Cross River (south-east, in Cross River State, with two sections), Gashaka-Gumti (east, in Taraba and Adamawa States on the Cameroon border), Chad Basin (north-east, in Borno and Yobe States, several small sections), Kamuku (north-central, in Kaduna State), and Yankari Game Reserve (north-east, in Bauchi State) shown with a different symbol (an orange marker). Rivers Niger and Benue and Lake Chad drawn in blue.

A two-panel illustration of resources and their conservation. Left panel "Renewable resources": a forest with a person planting a seedling, a river with a dam and a rainwater tank on a house, an elephant and antelope in a fenced protected area, and a farm with contour ridges and mulch. Right panel "Non-renewable resources": an oil well and a pipeline, a coal heap and a mine being refilled and replanted, a recycling bin with metal cans and glass bottles, and a roof with solar panels and a wind turbine as alternatives.

A three-stage illustration of desertification from left to right in northern Nigeria. Stage 1: green Sudan savanna with scattered trees, grass and a farm with crops. Stage 2: people cutting trees for firewood, a large herd of cattle and goats overgrazing, a bush fire, and bare patches of soil. Stage 3: bare land with sand dunes advancing over a farm and half-buried mud houses, a dry well and dust blowing in the wind. Warm sandy colours.

A view of a dry northern Nigerian landscape protected by a shelterbelt. On the right, the harmattan wind shown as arrows carrying sand from a desert area towards the left. In the middle, a long belt of several rows of trees (neem, acacia and eucalyptus) planted across the wind direction. On the left, behind the shelterbelt, a protected green farm with millet, a village and grazing animals. Sand is shown piling up against the windward side of the trees.
